After two months of daily use, the Keyrise K75 has earned a permanent place on my desk. At around eighty dollars, it sits comfortably in the mid-range category, but it offers many features you would expect from more expensive models.

The build quality is impressive. The aluminum top plate feels solid, and there is virtually no flex when typing. The pre-lubed linear switches are smooth and satisfyingly quiet, making this keyboard a great choice for shared offices. The PBT keycaps have a pleasant texture and show no signs of shine so far.

Connectivity is another highlight. You can switch between Bluetooth and a wired connection with ease, and the battery lasts around three weeks on a single charge. The companion software is simple to use and lets you remap keys without hassle.

There are a few drawbacks. The stabilizers on the spacebar rattle slightly, and the backlighting is not as bright as some competitors. Still, these are minor issues. Overall, the Keyrise K75 delivers excellent value, and I would happily recommend it to anyone looking to upgrade their typing experience without breaking the bank.
